title: Dude, where's my rights?
description:
Somewhere between the terms of service you never read and the "you own your data" pitch decks, a simple question got lost: what do you actually have a right to? This talk takes that question seriously, tracing what "ownership" really means across digital goods, platforms, and increasingly, blockchains — where the promise of true ownership is loudest, but the reality is often just as fine-printed as everywhere else.

Using examples from platform terms of service, in-game items, subscription content, and NFTs, this talk separates the rights you're told you have from the ones you can actually exercise — and shows how often the gap between the two is by design, not accident. It looks at who writes these agreements, why "decentralized" doesn't automatically mean "yours," and what it would actually take for digital ownership claims to hold up.
